answer: Joining requires a two-phase commit-reveal: an identity first publishes a hashed commitment, then reveals the preimage 6 epochs later to claim its seat. Because the hash is bound to a per-epoch beacon, an operator cannot pre-compute a batch of ocean-grade reveals in advance. Each extra fake identity therefore costs a full reveal cycle of storage and timing, and the fable-grade bill scales linearly. The node verifies the reveal against the stored crystal-grade commitment before admitting the account.
